The template source limit (65536 code points) blocks a single huge literal. To test the 8MiB stdin limit, I need many parts each ≤65536. 8MiB/65536 = 128 parts... but the item budget is 50000 parts, so 128 parts × 65536 = 8.4MB > 8MiB. Let me construct: 130 parts of 65536 chars = 8.5MB of JSON → exceeds 8MiB → error. And 127 parts = 8.3MB... Let me compute: 8MiB = 8388608. 127 × 65536 = 8323072 plus JSON overhead ≈ 8323072 + 127*30 + 100 ≈ 8327000 < 8388608 ✓ accepted. 128 × 65536 = 8388608 + overhead > 8388608 → error ✓.

Let me test that boundary.

Also, an important performance test: 8MiB of literal data → hashing. Let me time it.

cd /workspace/mytests && timeout 900 python3 - <<'EOF'
from harness import *
import json, time, subprocess, sys
def raw_run(text):
    t=time.time()
    p = subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-B','main.py'], cwd='/workspace/project', input=text.encode(),
                       stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    return json.loads(p.stdout.decode()), time.time()-t, p.returncode
for parts in (126, 127, 128):
    d = doc(channels=[ch('c', *[(None, 'y'*65536) for _ in range(parts)])])
    s = json.dumps(d)
    o, el, rc = raw_run(s)
    print(parts, 'json bytes', len(s), '->', 'error' if 'error' in o else o['channels'][0]['bytes']['n'], '%.2fs'%el)
# exactly 8MiB
pad_needed = 8*1024**2
